title: Property Tax Calculator: how it works, formula and examples

content:
The [Property Tax Calculator](/property-tax-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Annual and monthly property tax from home value and tax rate. Enter your home value and property tax rate and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Estimate your property tax from your home's value and the local tax rate. Property tax is usually charged by the county or town as a percentage of the assessed value, and it is normally paid monthly as part of the mortgage payment (the lender holds it in escrow) or directly twice a year. Rates vary enormously by location — under 0.5% in some states, over 2% in others — so the result is only as good as the rate you enter, and it is an estimate, not a bill.

## How to use the Property Tax Calculator

Start by entering your home value ($), then entering your property tax rate (%). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Enter your home's assessed value (usually close to its market value).
2. Enter your local tax rate as a percentage — check your county's website if you are unsure.
3. Read the annual, monthly and weekly tax.

## Formula

Annual tax = home value × tax rate. Monthly tax = annual tax ÷ 12. For example, a $400,000 home at 1.1% pays $4,400 a year, or about $367 a month.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Property Tax Calculator](/property-tax-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A $400,000 home taxed at 1.1% owes $4,400 a year — $366.67 a month, or $11 per $1,000 of value. Try the same figures in the [Property Tax Calculator](/property-tax-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Home value: 400000 $, Property tax rate: 1.1 %), the [Property Tax Calculator](/property-tax-calculator) returns Annual property tax: $4,400, Monthly property tax: $366.67, Weekly property tax: $84.62, Tax per $1,000 of value: $11. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Assessed value is not always market value

The tax is charged on the assessed value, which is the county's estimate of what the home is worth — and it is often lower than the sale price, sometimes much lower. Some places also cap how fast the assessed value can rise each year, or exempt part of it (a homestead exemption). If the assessed value on your tax bill differs from the market value, use the assessed value here.

## Rates vary by location

US property tax rates run from under 0.3% of value a year in Hawaii and Alabama to over 2% in New Jersey, Illinois and Connecticut — a sevenfold difference. Within a state, rates vary by county, school district and town. The average effective rate nationally is roughly 1%, but check your own county: the rate on your tax bill is the one that matters.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Use the assessed value from your tax bill, not the sale price.
- Check your county's rate — it varies far more than most people expect.
- Appeal the assessment if you think the value is too high.

## Frequently asked questions

### How is property tax calculated?

Home value × tax rate. A $400,000 home at 1.1% pays $4,400 a year. The rate is set by your county, town and school district. Try it with your own numbers in the [Property Tax Calculator](/property-tax-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What is a typical property tax rate?

The national average is roughly 1% of value a year, but it ranges from under 0.3% to over 2% depending on the state and county. Try it with your own numbers in the [Property Tax Calculator](/property-tax-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Do I pay property tax monthly?

Usually yes, as part of your mortgage payment — the lender collects it monthly and holds it in escrow, then pays the bill for you. Without a mortgage you normally pay directly, once or twice a year. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [Property Tax Calculator](/property-tax-calculator) and start straight away.

### Can I lower my property tax?

Sometimes: check for exemptions (homestead, senior, veteran), and appeal the assessed value if you can show similar homes are assessed lower. Try it with your own numbers in the [Property Tax Calculator](/property-tax-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
